themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 8 complaints THIS WEEK versus a 1.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% spike—suggesting either a new enforcement crackdown, illegal vending surge, or both in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 6.97)
Statistically significant spike with high severity classification
No prior Reddit or news coverage of vendor issues in district, suggesting emerging situation
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and local business owners: Is NYPD or Department of Consumer Affairs conducting a new enforcement sweep? What triggered it?
Check with Community Board 9 and local Council office on whether vendor complaints from residents prompted enforcement action

themes_detail.label: Obstructions blocking sidewalks/streets
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 6 complaints THIS WEEK from a 1.5-complaint weekly baseline—a 300% spike with z-score of 3.4—indicating a new or worsening problem with blocked pedestrian or vehicular pathways.
evidence: 6 obstruction complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.4)
Community Board repeatedly requests DOT capital funding for street infrastructure, suggesting long-standing pathway concerns
No recent news coverage, indicating this is emerging news
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaints this week—are they clustered around a specific block or transit corridor (e.g., near subway stations)?
Interview residents: Are vendors, construction equipment, or vehicle parking blocking sidewalks in specific hotspots?

themes_detail.label: Park rules violations escalating
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violation complaints exploded to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.2-complaint weekly average—a 1500% spike with z-score of 8.66 (highest severity)—but no recent news coverage or Reddit discussion, suggesting underreported emerging issue.
evidence: 4 park rules violations 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66—highest spike in dataset)
No Reddit or local news mentions of park safety issues, indicating potential news gap
Community Board requests park/playground upgrades, linking to broader park maintenance concerns
reporting_angles: Which parks are affected? (Morningside Park, St. Nicholas Terrace Park, or others?) What specific violations are being reported?
Interview Parks Department and precinct: Has there been a spike in unruly behavior, illegal activities, or safety incidents prompting complaints?

themes_detail.label: Water quality concerns emerging
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.4-complaint weekly average—a 700% increase with z-score of 5.42—pointing to potential contamination, discoloration, or odor issues affecting a subset of residents.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Heat/hot water remains the top complaint category overall (2,925 in 90 days), suggesting building infrastructure stress may be contributing to water system issues
No news coverage yet—water quality spikes can indicate infrastructure failure or contamination events
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection: Have they detected contamination, water main breaks, or boil-water notices in the district in the past 2 weeks?
Interview affected residents: What does the water look like/smell like? Is it specific to certain buildings or blocks (suggesting localized plumbing vs. citywide water system issue)?

themes_detail.label: Food safety incident cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago from a 0.2-complaint weekly average—a 1100% spike—but the timeframe is aging; however, no follow-up investigation in local news suggests potential underreporting of a restaurant or food vendor outbreak.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Vendor enforcement complaints also spiking THIS WEEK (8 vs. 1.2 baseline), suggesting possible food vendor enforcement sweep or contamination response
No news coverage of outbreak, creating reporting opportunity
reporting_angles: DOHMH follow-up: Did the 3 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago originate from a single restaurant or vendor? Was enforcement action taken?
Cross-reference vendor enforcement spike THIS WEEK with food poisoning spike 3 weeks ago—is the city responding to a known contamination event?
